action: Government, telecom and critical infrastructure security teams: load Check Point's published indicators, hunt for the listed registry and firewall artifacts, and warn staff that a browser certificate error offering a fix installer is a lure.
actor: CopperDragon (tool developer for China-nexus groups, moderate confidence)
exec: Shared tooling across China-linked espionage groups means a detection for one campaign may help against the others.
plain: Check Point found that three separate spying campaigns in Europe, Asia and Latin America used related malicious software from one developer, which appears to supply several China-linked hacking groups.

key_findings: Check Point tracks the builder of the Sparrow framework as CopperDragon, a possible tool supplier to China-nexus groups including FamousSparrow, Earth Estries and Tropic Trooper; confidence is moderate.
SilentDelivery hit government, shipping and IT targets in Europe and Asia from early 2026 using watering-hole sites with a fake Chrome certificate error and a bogus fix installer.
OceanGate targeted government and critical infrastructure in Asia through an internet-facing Linux server, then RDP password attempts against Windows administrators.
DarkWire has targeted telecom providers and foreign affairs and justice ministries in Latin America since mid-2025; its link to the group is weaker.
New tools include SquadC, AnnobinDoor, SparrowShell with an embedded Linux kernel rootkit, CopperDNS, and a passive backdoor hiding on a legitimate port.
recommendations: Hunt for the host artifacts Check Point lists, including a WindowsUpdateAssist Run key and firewall rules named RasiUwpApp and ss1.
Check for an unexpected LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy change and an account named admin$.
Load the published hashes, domains, addresses and certificate details into detection.

summary: Check Point Research links three espionage campaigns through the Sparrow malware framework, whose builder it tracks as CopperDragon, a possible tool supplier to several China-nexus groups. SilentDelivery used watering-hole sites in Europe and Asia, OceanGate hit government and critical infrastructure in Asia through Linux servers, and DarkWire targeted Latin American telecoms and ministries. Several backdoors and a Linux kernel rootkit are newly documented.
title: Three China-nexus espionage campaigns linked through Sparrow malware ecosystem

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Check Point Research report.
